interpretation.mcq: Options on published solution pages are read-only answer content, not an interactive quiz; no MCQ option buttons exist.
interpretation.solutionTabs: Question pages render their answer views as a tabset inside the existing .solution-body. Every panel ships visible and in source order, and solution-tabs.js then promotes the labels to a tablist with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation. A question with a single available view renders no tablist. Homepage labels remain a non-interactive illustrative group and stay out of the tab order.
interpretation.themeToggle: The header theme toggle was retired after this audit was first written; runs record themeTogglePresent so its absence is visible rather than silently passing.

The thumb then points downward (away from the observer below). Hence ω→ is directed downward.When the fan blades appear to rotate anticlockwise as seen from below, the right-hand rule gives ω directed downward (into the page from the observer). Since the speed is decreasing, α is directed upward, opposing ω.When the fan blades appear to rotate anticlockwise as seen from below, the right-hand rule gives ω directed downward (into the floor). Since speed is decreasing, α opposes ω and points upward (toward the ceiling).Since the speed is decreasing, the angular acceleration α→ opposes ω→, so α→ is directed upward.Therefore, angular velocity is downward and angular acceleration is upward.

Step-by-stepStep 1GivenDiameter of wheel = 1m → radius r = 0.5m; initial frequency n₀ = 0 rev/s (starts from rest); final frequency n = 2 rev/s; time t = 10s.Step 2Angular acceleration (in rev/s²)Since angular acceleration is uniform and the wheel starts from rest, we find the angular acceleration in convenient units of rev/s².α=n−n0t=2−010=0.2rev/s2Step 3Formula for number of revolutionsUsing the rotational kinematic equation analogous to s = u·t + ½·a·t², where N is the number of revolutions.N=n0t+12αt2Step 4Substitution – total revolutionsSubstitute n₀ = 0, α = 0.2 rev/s², t = 10s.N=0×10+12×0.2×(10)2Step 5Calculation – total revolutionsEvaluate the expression.N=12×0.2×100=10revolutionsStep 6Formula – time for the N-th completed revolutionRearranging N = ½·α·t² (since n₀ = 0) gives the time at which exactly N full revolutions are completed.tN=2NαStep 7Substitution – time for 1st complete revolutionSet N = 1, α = 0.2 rev/s².t1=2×10.2=10Step 8Calculation – time for 1st complete revolutionEvaluate numerically.t1=10≈3.16sStep 9Substitution – time at which 9th revolution is completedThe last (10th) revolution begins after 9 revolutions are done. Find t₉.t9=2×90.2=90=310Step 10Calculation – t₉Evaluate numerically.t9=310≈9.487sStep 11Time for last (10th) complete revolutionThe last revolution occupies the interval from t₉ to t₁₀ = 10s.Δtlast=t10−t9=10−310≈10−9.487≈0.51sFinal answerThe ant completes 10 revolutions in 10s.Time for the first complete revolution: t₁ = √10 ≈ 3.16s.Time for the last (10th) complete revolution: Δt = 10 − 3√10 ≈ 0.51s.
